title: U.S. Export Controls Fuel the Rise of Asian Data Centers Serving Chinese AI - The Wire China
gist: Paywalled teaser: Chinese AI firms are looking to Asian data centers (pictured: DayOne's Johor, Malaysia facility) where advanced chips are accessible; the body naming the beneficiary company is behind the paywall.

insights.claim: Chinese AI firms have been turning to data centers elsewhere in Asia to gain access to compute powered by the world's most advanced chips.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Southeast Asian data-center operators may capture Chinese AI demand seeking advanced-chip access; also a regulatory-risk vector for them.
insights.quote: Chinese AI firms have been looking to Asia for access to data centers powered by the world’s most advanced chips.
insights.locator: Chinese AI firms have been looking

insights.claim: DayOne operates a data center in Nusajaya Tech Park in Iskandar Puteri, Johor, Malaysia, which the article features as illustrating the Asian data-center buildout serving Chinese AI demand.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Johor is a hub to watch for both data-center growth and possible export-control enforcement scrutiny.
